::: {#def-bipartite-npsem-ie .theorem}
## Bipartite random network NPSEM [BRNNPSEM]

An RNNPSEM that represents a causal system with two classes of observational unit, $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, for example people and places, and edges only between classes: its structural equations fall into two groups, one for each class, and its graph generators produce bipartite graphs, in which a tie between a unit of $\mathcal{P}$ and a unit of $\mathcal{Q}$ runs both ways with the same weight:

$$
\psi_t(i,j)>0\Rightarrow i\text{ and }j\text{ are in distinct classes},\qquad \psi_t(i,j)=\psi_t(j,i)\ \text{ for } i\in\mathcal{P},\ j\in\mathcal{Q}.
$$

The adjacency matrix is therefore determined by the rows of the units in $\mathcal{P}$. For each graph generator, the network weights of a unit $i\in\mathcal{P}$ form a vector, $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{ti}=[\psi_t(i,l)]_{l\in\mathcal{Q}}\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{Q}|}$, taken as a single variable belonging to its observational unit, so that its equation is a structural equation of unit $i$: the relational equations of the BRNNPSEM become structural equations of the units in $\mathcal{P}$:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{ti}\in\mathscr{O}_i,\qquad \mathbf{V}=\bigcup_{i\in\mathcal{N}}\mathscr{O}_i.
$$

As a variable of unit $i$, the row is subject to equivalence (C.6), no contagion (C.14), identical structural distributions (C.16) and single-world independence (C.13). Homogeneous random network interference (C.25) continues to restrict only the equations of the covariates, as it did when the row’s entries were relational variables; how a row depends on the rest of the system is restricted instead by local row formation (C.29) or local tie formation (C.31).
:::
